text:
matt: Quick sync — proposing a different approach for autoscaler guardrails to reduce churn during short marketing-driven spikes. TL;DR: introduce a small, accountable 'surge credit' pool + adaptive cooldown that decays based on observed sequence length and egress pressure. Will sketch numbers below.

sophia: curious — how is this different from current burst-window + reserve?

matt: Good Q. Current model: static burst_window=10m, steady_reserve=15% per region. Problem: short 1-3m blasts consume burst and then we aggressively scale down then back up => oscillation and tradeoff in tail latency. New idea: give each pool a tiny surge_credit (measured in GPU-seconds) that absorbs microbursts without triggering full new nodes; if surge_credit exhausted, fallback to current burst behavior. Credit replenishes slowly and decays faster if network/egress is hot.

priya: sounds promising. Any numbers from experiments?

matt: Ran a quick loadgen yesterday against eu-west pool: baseline (current config) vs proto. Results (30m run, mixed short and long requests):
- baseline: 12.1 GPU-hours consumed, 99p latency 1.9s, observed 8 full node joins
- proto (surge_credit=1800s per-pool, cooldown=120s adaptive): 12.6 GPU-hours, 99p latency 1.48s, 2 full node joins, +5% cost.
Interpretation: small GPU-hour bump, large reduction in join churn/tail latency.

jordan: nice. Did you simulate cross-region fallback? remember last month apac fallback to eu caused egress saturation.

matt: I included a network pressure check — if egress > 70% for pool, decay rate for credit triples so we stop borrowing. In the test we triggered decay once and it prevented cross-region borrow.

priya: can we express this in Autoscaler config? share a minimal snippet so we can review.

matt: sure — pasted prototype config: 
```yaml
policy: multi_band
steady_reserve_pct: 15
surge_credit_seconds: 1800 # per-pool budget for microbursts
surge_replenish_rate: 300 # seconds to add 1s of credit back
adaptive_cooldown: true
cooldown_base: 120s
cooldown_decay: |
  if network_egress_pct > 70 -> multiply cooldown by 0.5 and accelerate credit decay
  if avg_seq_len > 512 -> increase cooldown by 1.5x
region_fallback_threshold: 0.8 # only fallback if local pool utilization > 80%
```

sophia: two asks: 1) add per-tenant caps so a noisy tenant can't drain pool credit, 2) metric to track: credit_consumed, credit_replenish_rate, credit_decay_events.

matt: agreed. Will add per-tenant cap and metrics. Also thinking of a small soft-queue that holds <= 5k tokens and serves from cache to avoid join pressure for tiny requests.

jordan: we should also add an egress-cost-signal so finance can veto if egress costs spike during a campaign. Maybe a safety switch: if projected daily egress delta > $X then block region borrow.

priya: ops question — how do we roll this? canary on one pool for 48h, then grad roll with 1h monitoring window?

matt: plan: canary on eu-west-1 pool for 48h during an expected low-traffic window, with a synthetic loadgen running a representative mix and production shadow traffic. If metrics (join_count, 99p latency, egress_pct) show improvement without cost > 8% we proceed. I'll open the rollout playbook PR after we agree.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: autoscaler/proto/surge-credit -> canary(eu-west-1).initiated by matt (CI job 6421).

sophia: reminder: add a dashboard tile for Credit Burn Rate + per-tenant top consumers. Also add an alert: sustained credit burn > 60% in 30m -> page oncall.

priya: one more risk: long-running background batch jobs might steadily shrink credit. Suggest excluding known batch tags from surge accounting.

matt: good call — will exclude tag:batch:nightly from credit accounting.

jordan: last note — make sure we don't accidentally change weighting for reserved vs preemptible; want to keep preemptible mix for cost. If surge_credit forces too many reserved node starts we lose cost benefits. Add cost-profile check in decision path.

matt: yep, decision path will prefer preemptible up to 60% of added capacity, only fall back to reserved if preemptible unavailable for >90s.

sophia: 👍 if you push the PR, ping me and i'll review dashboard panels.

matt: will do. Action items: matt -> PR with config + tagging + metrics; sophia -> dashboard panels; priya -> tenant cap list; jordan -> egress-cost safety thresholds. Canary start: scheduled 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC.

matt: thanks all :rocket:
